mg2_kealwea_10.m: Ten fragments of that burning star scattered along Galmore's bones. They are still warm. Still ... humming.
r: How do you know there are ten pieces?
Ten tongues of light, each flickering in defiance of the dark.
Teccow, a stargazer in Stoutford, told me so. Now go on.
You can feel that there are ten? Wow.

mg2_kealwea_14.m: [Ominous voice] In The Ash I Saw Them - Ten Tongues Of Light, Each Flickering In Defiance Of The Dark.

mg2_kealwea_15.m: Their Number Is Ten. Not Nine. Not Eleven. Ten.

mg2_kealwea_16.m: So if you have no more questions ...
r: Well, why don't you go and collect them?

mg2_kealwea_17.m: Only little children could ask such a stupid question. Of course I can't go. Sullengard needs me here.

mg2_kealwea_18.m: 'Yes. Bring these shards to me. Before the mountain's curse draws worse than beasts to them!
r: In fact I was already there.

mg2_kealwea_2.m: You saw it too, didn't you?
r: No, I haven't had any mead today.

mg2_kealwea_20.m: Kid, anything new about those fallen lights over Mt.Galmore?
r: I haven't found any pieces yet.
Here I have some pieces already.
I might give you half of them - five pieces.
I might give you the rest of them - five pieces.
I have found all of the ten pieces.
I have found all of the ten pieces, but I have already given them to Teccow in Stoutford.
I need some help of the local priest.

mg2_kealwea_25.m: You must be out of your mind! They are deadly - let me destroy all of them.
r: OK, you are right. Here take them and do what you must.
No, I will give you only half of them.

mg2_kealwea_26.m: Well, I am going to destroy these five. I hope you will be careful with the others and don't rue your decision.
r: I might throw the remaining ones at Andor. Hmm ...

mg2_kealwea_28.m: Good, good. I'll destroy these dangerous things.
r: Great to hear. And now I have to go and find my brother at last.

mg2_kealwea_3.m: There was a tear in the heavens. Not a star falling, but something cast down.

mg2_kealwea_30.m: Good, good. Give them to me. I'll destroy these dangerous things.
r: I seem to have lost them. Just a minute, I'll look for them ...
But I have already given them to Teccow in Stoutford.
Here you go. Take it and do what you have to do.
I've changed my mind. These glittery things are too pretty to be destroyed.
Hmm, I still have to think about it. I'll be back...

mg2_kealwea_4.m: It wept fire. And the mountain answered with a shudder. Such things are not random.

mg2_kealwea_40.m: You must be out of your mind! Free yourself from them or you are lost!
r: You are certainly right. Take it and do what you have to do.

mg2_kealwea_5.m: He gestured to the dark Galmore montains in the distant west.

mg2_kealwea_50.m: Wonderful. You have no idea what terrible things this crystal could have done.

mg2_kealwea_52.m: You did the right thing. The whole world is grateful to you.
r: I do something like that every other day.
I can't buy anything with words of thanks.

mg2_kealwea_56.m: I can't give you any gold. That belongs to the church.

mg2_kealwea_60.m: But this little book might bring you joy. Wait, I'll write you a dedication inside.

r: Enough, please! I can't think when you are talking like this.

mg2_starwatcher_19a.m: So you really don't want to help? And save the world from this disaster?
r: Maybe later. I have to go now.
No, I have enough other things to do.

mg2_starwatcher_19b.m: Woe, woe! Then leave me. I hope you can live with the guilt.

mg2_starwatcher_22.m: Don't waste time. Go again and find them. It is urgent!

mg2_starwatcher_24.m: Good, good. But these are not all of them. It must be ten - where are the others?

r: It was the right thing to do.

mg2_starwatcher_34.m: It is bad. But I won't talk about it anymore.

r: Now you're exaggerating. I'll go then.

sullengard_kealwea_0.m: Ah, young traveller. I am Kealwea. How can I help you, my child?
r: I am in need of supplies. Can you help?
Nanette told me to see you about her pond.
Mayor Ale has asked me to give this letter to you.
I am searching for something called "The Ritual of Five Aspects". I was told it may have passed through this town long ago.

sullengard_kealwea_kazaul_1.m: "The Ritual of Five Aspects"? That is not a name I hear often, my child. Some years back, when I first took stewardship of this church, I found mention of a strange relic - a bundle of parchment in an unknown tongue. It was sent north to the library in Remgard for study.
r: Do you remember who sent it there?
So it was once here in Sullengard?

sullengard_kealwea_kazaul_2.m: It was before my time, but the records say it came from one of my predecessors, the first priest to serve under the banner of the Shadow here. He noted that it was delivered to him by travelers claiming to have found it among the ruins to the west.
r: Ruins to the west, perhaps where Varnel perished.

sullengard_kealwea_kazaul_3.m: So it seems. It rested in our archives for generations, though no one could read it. When the scholars from Remgard offered to take it, we gladly let them. It felt unsettling to keep something no one understood.
r: Then Remgard is where I must go next.

sullengard_kealwea_kazaul_4.m: If you seek that ritual, Remgard's church library is where your path leads.

sullengard_kealwea_letter.m: Oh, I've been expecting this. Thank you.

sullengard_kealwea_pond_safety_1.m: [Sigh]. Yes, she told me about her pond as well, but she won't listen to my story.
r: I will listen to your story.
That will be a long story.

sullengard_kealwea_pond_safety_2.m: I used to go there when I was a young disciple.

sullengard_kealwea_pond_safety_3.m: One time, I was sitting on the bench thinking about how the Feygard soldiers can sleep at night with all of their unlawful taxes placed on the citizens of Sullengard causing all this financial trouble on the people.

sullengard_kealwea_pond_safety_4.m: My anger arose to the point that I lifted up a large rock and threw it in the pond.

sullengard_kealwea_pond_safety_5.m: After that, I saw some snappers emerge from the pond and attack me before I even realized what had happened. Good thing they are too slow to catch me as I quickly composed myself and limped home.

sullengard_kealwea_pond_safety_6.m: The moral of my story is to never again to throw rocks there, be it small or large. Thank you for listening. Please talk to Nanette about this.
r: Oh, I understand now. I have to tell her about this one. Bye
Oh, good thing it's not a long story. I'm about to start snoring here. Bye.

sullengard_kealwea_sell.m: Of course my child. Here, let's take a look at what I have.

beer_bootlegging.10: I've agreed to help the Feygard patrol captain investigate why there is so much beer on the Foaming flask tavern property.
beer_bootlegging.20: After bribing Torilo, the owner of the Foaming flask, he stated that he and other tavern owners had a 'business agreement' with a group of 'distributors'. He suggested that I ask other tavern owners for more information.
beer_bootlegging.30: After bribing Tharwyn, the owner of the Vilegard tavern, he stated as part of his 'business agreement', Dunla, the local thief, is one of his 'distributors'. He suggested that I talk to him.
beer_bootlegging.40: Dunla, the thief in Vilegard instructed me to speak with Farrick if I want to learn more about the tavern owner's 'business agreement' with their 'distributors'.
beer_bootlegging.50: Farrik told me that the beer is coming from Sullengard. I really should go there next.
beer_bootlegging.60: To earn his trust, Mayor Ale has asked that I deliver his letter to Kealwea, the Sullengard priest.
beer_bootlegging.70: I have done what Mayor Ale has asked of me as I have delivered his letter. I should now return to him.
beer_bootlegging.80: Mayor Ale has explained everything to me about the 'business agreement' with the Thieves guild. I should head back to the Foaming flask tavern and speak with the captain.
beer_bootlegging.90: I informed the guard captain at the Foaming flask tavern all about the beer bootlegging operation.
beer_bootlegging.100: I informed the guard captain at the Foaming flask tavern that the beer was being distributed by the Thieves guild.
beer_bootlegging.110: I informed the guard captain at the Foaming flask tavern that Sullengard was responsible for brewing the beer.
beer_bootlegging.120: I lied to the guard captain at the Foaming flask tavern and told him nothing about the beer bootlegging operation.

sullengard_pond_safety.10: Nanette was troubled that her pond is unsafe because of the monsters that emerged in the pond.
sullengard_pond_safety.20: I accepted her request to clear out the monsters in her pond area so that she could enjoy the pond again.
sullengard_pond_safety.30: I have now cleared the pond area. Nanette told me that I should talk to Kaelwea, the priest of Sullengard, to see if he has some information about the cause of the monster's appearance in the pond area.
sullengard_pond_safety.40: The priest Kaelwea told me a story about his strange experience same as Nanette's experience in the pond area. I should better tell her the moral of the story.
sullengard_pond_safety.50: I told Nanette the moral of the story. She had already learned from her mistake and she promised never to do it again just to release her anger issue against the unfair taxes of Feygard.

fifth_master.10: In Undertell, the Kazaul Masters spoke to me. They claimed a forgotten ritual could seal the Rift once and for all.
fifth_master.20: They told me that this ritual was stolen long ago by a Lethgar named Varnel, who fled Undertell with it. I agreed to recover it, believing it might save Dhayavar.
fifth_master.30: In the upper dormitory tunnels of Undertell, I met the ghost of a miner who remembered Varnel. The ghost said Varnel escaped through the northern caverns and headed east toward the Sutdover River. Could he have meant Sullengard?
fifth_master.40: I traveled to Sullengard and spoke with Kealwea, the local priest. He recalled a relic matching my description once being sent to the Shadow church library in Remgard.
fifth_master.50: In Remgard's church basement, I spoke with Gwendolyn, the librarian. She said she knew nothing of any ritual but allowed me to search the shelves myself.
fifth_master.55: I discovered a small, locked box hidden behind the books. Its surface was etched with strange curling runes and old scorch marks. The box refused to open.
fifth_master.58: After I asked Gwendolyn about the locked box that I found, she directed me to speak with Skylenar upstairs.
fifth_master.60: Skylenar told me the box was an ancient relic, sealed by dragonkind and said to open only to a dragon's claw.
fifth_master.65: Skylenar mentioned that some old Shadow tales spoke of ash-covered scales found deep within Undertell, hinting that one such beast may once have lived there.
fifth_master.70: In the glowing white house basement, I talked to Falkour the dragon. When I showed him the locked box, he recognized it as a relic once held by Varnel.
fifth_master.72: Falkour gifted me one of his claws, saying it could break the seal, and warned me to use it only for that purpose. Time to find a safe place in this basement to open the box.
fifth_master.75: Using Falkour's claw, I unlocked the ancient box. Inside were the five pages of the Kazaul ritual the Masters desired.
fifth_master.78: The Master that I brought "The Five Aspects" ritual to sent me to talk to Thalen, the Master of Knowledge.
fifth_master.80: I returned the ritual to Thalen. He told me to meet the "lesser kin" at Anavrin's shrine to perform the ceremony.
fifth_master.85: As the ritual completed, the Masters revealed their true intent. The rite was not to seal the Rift but to awaken the Fifth Master, whose power might reopen it. They told me the Shadow itself serves Kazaul. Their words left me doubtful, unsure whether I had been deceived or warned.
fifth_master.90: I left Undertell uncertain of what to believe. If what the Masters said is true, the Shadow may not be what it seems. Still, doubt lingers like smoke after the forge cools.
